# FREE SECURITY TOOLS

Standalone tools you can download and run right now — no account required, nothing sent to a server. Plus a vulnerability scanner that runs in this website (free account).

## Browser Guard

What's new in 0.4.3 : A step-by-step guide and a ? help box for every setting in the toolbar pop-up, including what the optional reporting sends and never sends. Since 0.4.0 it detects current API key formats, hides the secret in its warning, and is hardened against web pages that try to slow it down or tamper with it.

Screens the AI chats and LLM apps you use for prompt-injection and jailbreak attempts the moment you send them — flags risky prompts inline, right on the page. Runs entirely in your browser, non-blocking.

Prefer one file? The userscript installs straight into Tampermonkey / Violentmonkey — no unpacking.

The macOS bundle is the same extension in a disk image, not a separate Mac app — you still load it into your browser.

## Aegis — AI Security Scanner

A single ~8 MB binary that finds real misconfigurations across Windows, macOS, and Linux. Read-only , runs fully offline / air-gapped, zero dependencies, and maps findings to CIS and MITRE ATT&CK — a prioritized report in seconds.

## Pulse — What's Being Exploited Right Now

A small, read-only CLI that reads the software you actually run — by real package name and version — and tells you the few components that are being actively exploited in the wild, instead of dumping thousands of unranked CVEs. Powered by ThreatClaw's CISA KEV + EPSS intelligence. Matches fully offline — nothing about your host leaves the machine.

# rank an existing scan (Trivy / Grype / npm audit) — zero setup pulse triage trivy-report.json # or scan a project / the whole host (uses Trivy under the hood) pulse scan . # refresh the offline KEV + EPSS intel pulse update

triage needs nothing but an existing scan export. scan uses the open-source Trivy engine ( brew install trivy , apt install trivy , …). Add --fail-on kev to gate CI.

## Vulnerability Scanner

Drop a project folder, lockfiles, an SBOM or a container image archive. You get known flaws ranked by what is being exploited (CISA KEV, EPSS), a fix plan, secrets, misconfigurations, licences, and an SBOM to download. Files are read in your browser; only package names, versions and ecosystems are sent to ThreatClaw to look up known flaws, and nothing is saved.

## SBOM Builder

Make a CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM for a project or a container image. Your files stay on your machine. Encrypt it, sign it, and see which required fields it holds.
